correctness.rationale: The model y^3=x^5+a x^3+b x+1 is tame Kummer of degree 3 in characteristic 2: f=x f' +1 proves separability for every coefficient pair, five simple finite branch points and one at infinity give 2g-2=-6+12=6. The listed four differentials dx/y, dx/y², x dx/y², x² dx/y² are regular with infinity valuations (1,6,3,0), form a basis, and their semilinear Cartier map C(e1)=e4+sqrt(a)e3+sqrt(b)e2, C(e3)=e1, C(e2)=C(e4)=0 is obtained by extracting odd terms in f(x) dx. With w=C(e1), C(w)=a^(1/4)e1, so stable C^4-rank is zero exactly when a=0, otherwise two; rank C=2 throughout, so a-number 2. f'=(x²+sqrt(a)x+sqrt(b))² has 1 vs 2 distinct critical roots; count q coefficients with a=0 and q(q-1) elsewhere. This is set-theoretic, not a determinantal-scheme multiplicity. Independent GF(2) matrix rank powers for all (a,b) reproduce the four ranks; finite fields cannot prove the all-algebraically-closed classification.
